reference: Palladium-catalyzed Buchwald–Hartwig Amination and Suzuki–Miyaura Cross-coupling Reaction of Aryl Mesylates. Organic Syntheses, Vol. 92, pp. 195-212 (2015). DOI: 10.15227/orgsyn.092.0195. URL: https://www.orgsyn.org/demo.aspx?prep=v92p0195
experimental_procedure: In a resealable Schlenk flask under N2, Pd(OAc)2 (1.0 mol%) and CM‑Phos (4.0 mol%) are combined with DCM (18 mL) and Et3N (1.8 mL). After 5 min in a 50 °C oil bath, volatiles are removed (0.01 mmHg, 1 h). K2CO3 (2.5 equiv), phenylboronic acid (0.2 equiv), 4-(tert‑butyl)phenyl mesylate (1.0 equiv), N‑methylaniline (≈1.5 equiv), and tert‑butyl alcohol (70 mL) are added under N2. Stir 10 min at rt, then heat at 120 °C for 24 h. Work up by dilution/extraction, dry (Na2SO4), concentrate, and purify by silica gel chromatography (hexane then CH2Cl2/hexane 1:49) to afford the tertiary aniline.
notes: Second step (amination) only: Pd(OAc)2/CM-Phos-catalyzed Buchwald–Hartwig amination of 4-(tert-butyl)phenyl mesylate with N-methylaniline in tert-butanol at 120 °C for 24 h under N2. Catalyst pre-activation in DCM/Et3N, then solvent removal prior to coupling.
